---
title: "Acknowledgements"
subtitle: "The people who wrote it down."
---

The data in this project was not generated by a machine. Every record began as
a handwritten entry on a paper card, made by someone standing at a potting
bench, often with soil on their hands. This page recognizes the people whose
daily work created the archive that made this project possible.

## UBCBG Nursery propagation staff

The propagation cards span roughly fifty years of horticultural practice at
the University of British Columbia Botanical Garden Nursery. Over that time,
approximately twenty horticulturists, propagators, and nursery staff recorded
their work on these cards. Their handwriting is, quite literally, the raw
material of this project.

> *To be populated with individual acknowledgements as records are reviewed
> and staff identified. Many contributors can be recognized through initials
> and handwriting on the cards themselves.*

## UBC Botanical Garden

This work exists within the broader institutional context of the UBC Botanical
Garden, whose staff, administration, and volunteers, past and present, have
maintained the living collections for over a century. The Garden's commitment
to conservation, research, and public education provides the foundation on
which projects like this one are built.

## Open-source projects

The Propagation Card Reader is built entirely on open-source software. The
following projects made this work possible:

- **[Ollama](https://ollama.com/)** -- local model serving engine
- **[Qwen 2.5-VL](https://github.com/QwenLM/Qwen2.5-VL)** -- vision language model (Alibaba Qwen team)
- **[Gemma 3](https://ai.google.dev/gemma)** -- vision language model used during early development (Google DeepMind)
- **[OpenCV](https://opencv.org/)** -- computer vision library used in the template matching prototype
- **[PyMuPDF](https://pymupdf.readthedocs.io/)** -- PDF rendering and page extraction
- **[Quarto](https://quarto.org/)** -- this website
- **[SQLite](https://sqlite.org/)** -- database engine
- **[Python](https://python.org/)** and the broader scientific Python ecosystem

## Development tools

The final iteration of this project was developed using an agentic coding
workflow, with **Claude Opus 4.6** (Anthropic) as an orchestrator and the
**[OpenClaw](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw)** system as a local
development harness.
